symptoms: Water-soaked dark patches appear on leaves and stems, then the plant turns brown quickly. Fruit can show hard dark rot and the whole crop may collapse in wet weather.
cause: A fast-moving fungal-like disease that spreads in cool, wet conditions and in gardens with poor airflow.
cultural_control: Remove badly infected plants and keep them away from the garden. Stake plants, avoid watering the leaves, improve spacing, and destroy old infected crop debris after harvest.
chemical_option: Use only products registered in Uganda for tomato blight if needed, such as mancozeb or metalaxyl mixtures. Ask an agro-dealer or extension officer for the product and dose, wear protective clothing, and follow the pre-harvest interval on the label.
prevention: Keep the tomato garden airy and dry where possible, and ask NARO or your extension officer for current recommended varieties.
see_officer_when: Seek help quickly if wet weather is spreading the disease or many plants are collapsing in a short time.
